R005.BG003.fact: In a field K of prime characteristic p, an integer a has zero image exactly when p divides a. Hence if 0<=r<p, the integer r! has nonzero image in K, including 0!=1. A unital ring map R->K sends each unit of R to a unit of K, and therefore to a nonzero element.

kappa is shown to be a unital ring map extending the integer map.

R005.BG003.justification: Divide an integer by p; its image is the image of its remainder. By the defining minimal positive characteristic, no remainder from 1 through p-1 is zero, so the kernel is pZ. Every factor 1,...,r is consequently nonzero; a finite product of nonzero field elements is nonzero. For a unit t with inverse s, kappa(t)kappa(s)=1, so kappa(t) is invertible and cannot be zero in a field.
